patch_description: Replace the random-points placeholder with a deterministic construction plus a seeded stochastic local search that directly maximizes the normalized minimum triangle area. We initialize with a regular dodecagon plus its center (a strong symmetric baseline, since 3-fold/6-fold symmetric configurations are known to perform well on the Heilbronn problem), then run coordinate-perturbation hill climbing: repeatedly perturb one point, keep the move only if the ratio (min triangle area)/(convex hull area) improves. All triangle areas are computed vectorized via 2D cross products over all C(13,3)=286 triples, and the convex hull area via a monotonic-chain hull. A fixed seed and a fixed iteration schedule guarantee reproducibility. This should raise the normalized score from ~0 to roughly the 0.02-0.03 range, well above the trivial baseline.
